source.citation: Qiu XS et al. Anatomical Study of the Clavicles in a Chinese Population. Biomed Res Int. 2016:6219761.
source.measurement_definition: Straight 3D chord between central points of the two clavicular articular surfaces, source methods 2.1 item 1; not medial/lateral extrema or curved centreline.

male_chord_mm.sd_basis: per-bone (52 bilateral clavicles from 26 men); between-person SD is larger

source.population: 52 Chinese patients, 26 male/26 female; bilateral clavicles; mean age 49.8 ±18.2 y; no previous clavicle fracture
limitations: Bilateral bones are not 52 independent subjects.
Articular surface centre is not automatically instantaneous joint rotation centre.
No stature-conditioned regression; do not promote the mean to final anatomy.
Do not average this centre chord with extremal-point chords or centreline true lengths.

comparison.policy: Keep all three endpoint definitions separate; no inferred extrema-to-centre correction or same-subject chord/curve ratio.

SC_anchor_search.LI_2012_PMID_22340551: 53 healthy volunteers; abstract confirms bilateral clavicle distance was measured but omits that numeric result and exact endpoints. Full table/figure required; not used to freeze SC breadth.
SC_anchor_search.TUSCANO_2009_PMID_19308406: 104 CT cases; joint-space/head-diameter/anterior-offset variation, not bilateral SC-centre breadth. No SC anchor derived.
SC_anchor_search.WIJERATNA_2013_PMID_22933016: CT joint-plane study, 80 patients 25–40 y; manubrium/joint-plane orientation is not an SC-centre coordinate.

required_next: Endpoint-matched independent centre-chord evidence plus stature/context and manubrial articular landmarks; retain SC/AC/GH separation.
